claims.text: The OIG issued DODIG-2016-113 on 26 July 2016 finding $2.8 trillion in unsupported third quarter and $6.5 trillion in unsupported yearend journal voucher adjustments to Army General Fund data for FY2015.

claims.nodeLabel: DODIG-2016-113 - Army General Fund Adjustments Not Adequately Documented or Supported
claims.text: The report states that OASA(FM&C) and DFAS Indianapolis 'did not adequately support $2.8 trillion in third quarter journal voucher (JV) adjustments and $6.5 trillion in yearend JV adjustments made to AGF data during FY 2015 financial statement compilation.'

claims.nodeLabel: DODIG-2016-113 - Army General Fund Adjustments Not Adequately Documented or Supported
claims.text: Footnote 2 of the report states the amounts are not cumulative and should not be added together.

claims.nodeLabel: DODIG-2016-113 - Army General Fund Adjustments Not Adequately Documented or Supported
claims.text: The $6.5 trillion figure is the gross value of unsupported compilation adjustments, not an amount of missing money; the same dollars can be adjusted repeatedly within a compilation cycle. Reasoning: the Army General Fund's FY2015 appropriation was on the order of $120-150 billion, so a literal reading would require the Army to have handled roughly fifty times its own budget, which is arithmetically impossible; the figure therefore measures entry volume, not fund flow.
DoD OIG report DODIG-2016-113 found that Army General Fund adjustments were not adequately documented or supported.

claims.nodeLabel: Summary Report on 'Unsupported Journal Voucher Adjustments' (Skidmore and Fitts, 2017)
claims.text: The $21 trillion figure double-counts by construction, because gross adjustment volumes across eighteen years are being summed and individual dollars are adjusted repeatedly; it is an index of documentation failure, not a quantity of money. Reasoning: it is derived from the same class of gross-entry figures as the DODIG-2016-113 $6.5 trillion number, which the OIG itself flags as non-cumulative.
